<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="right"><B>Exhibit 99.1 </B></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt" ALIGN="center">


<IMG SRC="g149126g0813081313021.jpg" ALT="LOGO">
 </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>Atrium Therapeutics Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>&#8212; IND clearance for ATR 1072 and launch of Corventis Phase 1/2 trial in </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>PRKAG2 syndrome &#8212; </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>&#8212; Achieved second milestone payment under global cardiovascular collaboration </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>with Bristol Myers Squibb &#8212; </I></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">SAN
DIEGO, August&nbsp;13, 2026 / PRNewswire/ &#8211; Atrium Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: RNA) (&#8220;Atrium,&#8221; &#8220;Atrium Therapeutics,&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;), a&nbsp;biopharmaceutical company&nbsp;advancing precision cardiology
by developing&nbsp;RNA therapeutics targeted&nbsp;to the heart, today reported financial results for the second quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2026, and highlighted recent corporate progress including FDA clearance of its Investigational New Drug (IND)
application for ATR 1072 and continued achievements under its collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#8220;Our team continues to execute well,
achieving FDA clearance of our IND for ATR 1072 and launching Corventis &#8212; Atrium&#8217;s first Phase 1/2 trial and the first clinical study to evaluate a potential disease-modifying treatment for people living with PRKAG2 syndrome,&#8221; said
Kathleen Gallagher, President and Chief Executive Officer of Atrium Therapeutics. &#8220;Atrium&#8217;s precision approach to genetic cardiomyopathies is part of a burgeoning frontier in medicine. Our experienced team is well-positioned to continue
advancing and efficiently expanding our pipeline with urgency on behalf of patients and clinicians.&#8221; </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Recent Highlights </B></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="5%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">&#149;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt"><B>Received FDA clearance of IND application and Health Canada No Objection Letter for ATR 1072. </B>FDA cleared
Atrium&#8217;s IND application for ATR 1072, allowing the Company to proceed with Corventis, a Phase 1/2 open-label, multicenter clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy of ATR
1072 in participants living with PRKAG2 syndrome. Additionally, the Company has received a No Objection Letter from Health Canada enabling the activation of planned Corventis study sites in Canada. The study will enroll approximately 37 participants
across two parts: Part A, multiple ascending dose cohorts to characterize safety and support dose selection, and Part B, a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">single-arm</FONT> expansion cohort at the recommended Phase 2 dose to further evaluate
efficacy trends in cardiac structure and function. ATR 1072 is Atrium&#8217;s first precision cardiology program to enter the clinic. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
</DIV></Center>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt"><B>Cash, Cash Equivalents, and Short-term Investments: </B>As of June&nbsp;30, 2026, Atrium $263.9&nbsp;million
in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments. The Company believes its current cash resources, inclusive of the receipt of the second milestone payment from had BMS earned in August, are sufficient to fund planned operations through <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">mid-2028.</FONT> </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About Atrium Therapeutics </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Atrium Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: RNA) is pioneering targeted delivery of ribonucleic acid (RNA) therapeutics to the heart to transform the standard of care
for people living with cardiomyopathies. With the U.S. Food and Drug Administration&#8217;s (FDA) recent clearance of its Investigational New Drug (IND) application for ATR 1072 for PRKAG2 (Protein Kinase
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">AMP-activated</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-catalytic</FONT> subunit Gamma 2) syndrome, Atrium is advancing its first precision cardiology program into the clinic through the Corventis Phase 1/2
clinical trial. The Company&#8217;s proprietary technology - designed at Avidity Biosciences, Inc. - combines the tissue selectivity of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and other targeted delivery ligands with the precision of oligonucleotides and is
designed to selectively target the underlying drivers of genetically driven cardiac diseases through targeted, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-viral</FONT> delivery of small interfering RNA (siRNA). This approach builds upon learnings from
demonstrated delivery to skeletal muscle and applies it for efficient delivery to the heart, with the potential to overcome challenges associated with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-specific</FONT> tissue delivery. Beyond ATR 1072, the
Company&#8217;s pipeline includes ATR 1086 for PLN (phospholamban) cardiomyopathy and two undisclosed research targets in rare cardiomyopathies. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For more
information about our RNA delivery platform, development pipeline and people, please visit https://atriumtherapeutics.com/ and engage with us on LinkedIn. </P>
</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt" ALIGN="center">


<IMG SRC="g149126g0813081313021.jpg" ALT="LOGO">
 </P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Availability of Other Information About Atrium Therapeutics </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Investors and others should note that&nbsp;Atrium Therapeutics&nbsp;communicates with its investors and the public using its
website&nbsp;https://atriumtherapeutics.com/, including, but not limited to,&nbsp;Atrium Therapeutics&#8217;&nbsp;disclosures, investor presentations and FAQs,&nbsp;Securities and Exchange Commission&nbsp;(&#8220;SEC&#8221;) filings, press releases,
public conference call transcripts and webcast transcripts, as well as on LinkedIn. The information that&nbsp;Atrium Therapeutics&nbsp;posts on its website or on LinkedIn could be deemed to be material information. As a result,&nbsp;Atrium
Therapeutics&nbsp;encourages investors, the media, and others interested to review the information that it posts there on a regular basis. The contents of&nbsp;Atrium Therapeutics&#8217;&nbsp;website or social media shall not be deemed incorporated
by reference in any filing under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About PRKAG2 Syndrome </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">PRKAG2 syndrome is a rare, autosomal dominant, early-onset cardiomyopathy caused by mutations in the PRKAG2 gene, which encodes the Gamma 2 regulatory subunit
of AMPK. Mutations enhance AMPK activity leading to abnormal glycogen accumulation in heart, thickened heart muscles, electrical conduction problems, and arrhythmias. Based on current scientific literature estimates, there are at least 1,000 &#8211;
2,000 people with PRKAG2 syndrome in the U.S. Current management is limited to symptomatic treatment; no approved therapies exist to address the underlying genetic driver of disease. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About PLN Cardiomyopathy </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Phospholamban
(&#8220;PLN&#8221;) cardiomyopathy is a rare autosomal dominant, progressive cardiac disease caused by mutations in PLN, a key regulator of sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase 2a (&#8220;SERCA2a&#8221;) calcium pump. PLN mutations produce protein
aggregates that disrupt endoplasmic reticulum processes and lead to dilated, arrhythmogenic, or hypertrophic cardiomyopathies and a significantly increased risk of heart failure and sudden cardiac death. There are 2,000 &#8211; 4,000 people with
pathogenic PLN variants in the United States. No approved therapies target the underlying molecular cause of the disease. </P>
</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
